chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who shot an arrow at a wild donkey or a deer and hit it, then he was in search of it and found it the next morning with his arrow in it. So he (peace be upon him) said: If he knows that he hit it and that his arrow is the one that killed it, then let him eat from it; otherwise, he should not eat from it.

key_terms.الْغَد: the next day/morning — indicating a time gap creating uncertainty
key_terms.حِمَارَ وَحْشٍ: wild donkey (onager) — a game animal that is halal to hunt
key_terms.ظَبْي: deer or gazelle — a common game animal
key_terms.قَتَلَ: killed — the key determination for lawfulness of the game

ai.seo_question: Is it halal to eat game found dead with an arrow the next day in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses a specific hunting scenario: when a hunter shoots an arrow at wild game, loses track of it, and finds it dead the next day. The ruling establishes that the hunter may eat the game only if he is certain that his arrow was responsible for the kill — uncertainty about cause of death renders the game forbidden. This reflects the Islamic jurisprudential principle that lawful slaughter (or lawful hunting) requires certainty, as the animal may have died from another cause during the night.

en.hubeali: A number of our companoins, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who shot (an arrow) at a wild donkey, or a deer, so it hit him. Then he was in search for it, so he found it in the morning, and his arrow was in it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he knows that he hit it, and that it was his arrow which killed it, so let him eat from it, or else, so he should not eat from it’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who shoots a wild donkey or a deer which is shot and he searches for it but finds it the next day with his arrow in it. He (the Imam) said, ‘If he knows that his shot had hit it and the arrow is his arrow which has killed it, he then can use it for food, otherwise, he cannot use it for food.’”
